title: Led in groups
hookLine: the mindful are led to the garden in groups, and greeted with peace (39:73)
tomorrow: Forgiver of sin, accepter of return

cards: Watch the doors of a wedding hall, a stadium, a graduation. People rarely arrive alone. They come in clusters: a family, a carload of friends, a team in matching shirts.
You can tell who belongs with whom by who they're walking beside. Surah thirty-nine is named for that. Zumar: groups, crowds, companies.
At its very end, it pictures the Day of Judgment not as a long line of individuals, but as people arriving in groups, and the gates they arrive at.

teach.b: Verse seventy-one: those who denied are driven toward hell in groups. When they arrive, its gates are opened, and its keepers ask: didn't messengers come to you?
Verse seventy-three: those mindful of their Lord are led to the garden in groups. When they arrive, and its gates have been opened, its keepers say: salamun 'alaykum, peace be upon you.
You've done well, so enter, to stay. Now a small detail in the Arabic. In the first verse, its gates are opened: futihat.
In the second, there's an extra and: wa futihat, and its gates have been opened.
Some commentators read that and as meaning the garden's gates were already open, waiting, like a host who unlocks the door before the guests reach the house.
And the first words are peace. Not a test, not a question. A greeting.
Elsewhere the Qur'an says each person comes to Him alone; here, at the gates, they arrive together. Then verse seventy-four: the people say, praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us.

teach.h: PRAISE TO THE LORD OF THE WORLDS.
teach.b: The surah ends with the angels circling the Throne, and the words: praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.

Look back across this week and the same arc shows: peace on all the messengers; Dawud bowing when he saw his mistake; Ayyub's spring after long illness; the sincere that Iblis can't reach; the one who prays at night and knows; mercy for those who'd gone too far.
And now groups of people walking together toward open gates, greeted with peace.

how: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu 'alaykum, peace be upon you, the same greeting the Qur'an says the angels give at the garden's gates, and are encouraged to keep good company.

o: groups or companies, people arriving together
the trumpet blast that opens the Last Day
a chorus of voices raised together in praise

games.q: the end of Az-Zumar — tap the pairs.
p: praise to the Lord of the Worlds

s: in Az-Zumar's last scene, people reach the gates one by one
they arrive in groups, zumar; elsewhere (19:95) each comes alone, but at these gates they come together.
the keepers of the garden greet the arrivals with peace
salamun 'alaykum: peace be upon you, you've done well.
many commentators read an extra 'and' as the gates already being open
wa futihat: like a host who opens the door before the guests arrive.

games.q: the mindful arrive at the garden in groups. the gates are open. what do the keepers say first?
games.why: peace be upon you. you've done well, so enter, to stay.

practice: Picture the people you spend most of your time with as a group, walking somewhere together. Which way are they walking, and who leaves you steadier than they found you?
Hold one of them in mind and, if you pray, thank God for them; if not, simply be grateful, and think of one person you'd like to walk beside more often.

wordCard.voice: Zumar: groups, crowds, companies, the name of the surah whose last verses picture the mindful led to the garden together. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: in groups, in companies, the word that names surah thirty-nine.

carryVoice: Your line: greeted with peace. A week of mercy ends at an open gate. Day five hundred sixty, and the week is done.

sources.ref: tafsir on 39:73 (the waw in wa futihat)
